title: Majestic Indian Peacock Motif Mehndi Design for Arm
descriptionParagraphs: A sophisticated indian mehndi design tailored for the arm, featuring bracelet cuff and ring pattern. Rated as Medium, this pattern is perfect for everyday.

Henna on the forearm stains lighter than on the palm because the skin is thinner. Arm designs are easier to apply on someone else than on yourself, especially past the wrist. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.

Indian mehndi varies significantly by region — Rajasthani, Gujarati, and South Indian styles each have distinct characteristics. In many Indian families, the bride does not perform household chores until her mehndi has fully faded.
Application tips: The stain starts orange and darkens to reddish brown over 24 to 48 hours as it oxidises. Wash and dry the skin before application and skip lotion or oil, which block the dye.

image.alt: Indian Peacock Motif mehndi design for arm — majestic henna pattern

faq.q: Why do Indian brides apply mehndi?
faq.a: Mehndi is considered auspicious in Indian culture. It symbolizes love, joy, and the bond between the bride and groom.

faq.q: How long should I leave Indian mehndi on for a dark stain?
faq.a: Leave the paste on for 6-8 hours (many brides leave it overnight). Apply a lemon-sugar sealant and keep hands warm.

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?
faq.a: A natural henna stain usually lasts one to three weeks. It fades faster on areas that are washed or rubbed often, such as the hands.
